claims.statement: Session Diffs is a git-backed capture protocol: the sandbox runtime compares each session repository checkout against an immutable pinned base commit and uploads one bounded patch bundle; the control plane SessionDO validates, stores, and serves it to the web client as a Changes panel.

Baseline SHAs are immutable: resolve_session_diff_baselines keeps supplied base_sha values and only discovers a missing one (git rev-parse HEAD) on the first boot; snapshot-restore boots never rediscover so the original session's baseline survives a restore.

The bridge advertises repository positions and baseSha values in the ready event; SessionDiffService.pinBaselines verifies the advertised list matches the session's configured repositories (same count, positions, case-insensitive identity) and writes base_sha only where the member row's column is NULL, mirroring the primary SHA into the session scalar.

For legacy sessions without member rows, SessionDiffService.getBaseline falls back to the scalar session.base_sha mirror for the primary repository, so older sessions still get a comparison point; a session whose repositories have no baseline at all reports unavailableReason 'Changes unavailable for this session' in the public state.

Git capture always uses argument arrays with a hardened helper: GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, LC_ALL=C, per-command stdout ceilings, and kill-on-timeout; repository paths and filenames are never interpolated into a shell command, and replacement refs cannot shift the baseline comparison.

Tracked changes come from git diff --raw -z --no-abbrev --find-renames <base_sha> plus --numstat and the --diff-filter=U name list; untracked files come from git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z filtered through checkout-local runtime excludes; per-file patches are rendered with --unified=1000000 (or --no-index against /dev/null for untracked files).

Runtime-installed files are excluded from capture through the managed info/exclude block (git_excludes.py): untracked runtime assets never appear as agent changes, tracked changes are never hidden by the excludes, and a staged deletion recreated as untracked at the same path is normalized into one modified metadata_only record.

Each captured file is classified into one of four render states serialized verbatim — renderable, metadata_only, too_large, binary — where metadata_only covers mode-only changes, pure renames, unmerged/overlay paths, submodule gitlinks, and empty patches, and binary is detected from git's '-' numstat columns.

Submodule gitlink changes are reported as status submodule metadata-only records carrying old/new commit pointers, resolved to the submodule's actual checked-out HEAD when git reports the all-zero dirty pointer.

Production capture limits are 1,000 files max, 512 KiB per patch, 1 MiB aggregate capture bytes, 1,572,864 bytes max encoded bundle, 8 MB per-command metadata ceiling, and a 20 s git command timeout; these mirror the shared TS constants SESSION_DIFF_MAX_* in packages/shared/src/types/session-diffs.ts.

If the encoded bundle exceeds its wire limit, _bound_encoded_bundle sheds the largest patches first (downgrading to too_large), then trailing metadata records (incrementing truncated and omittedFileCount), and only raises DiffCaptureError if even metadata alone cannot fit.

A repository whose capture fails is serialized as an unavailable upload with a bounded error string and empty file list so a multi-repository bundle still uploads atomically; if every repository is unavailable the worker reports a refresh failure instead of publishing an empty bundle.

SessionDiffRefreshWorker is a non-blocking, coalesced scheduler: request() only bumps a generation counter and spawns the collection task if none is running; refresh requests are held idle while prompts are active, and a collection that went stale (new prompt started or newer request) is discarded and retried against current state by the loop.

The bridge triggers a diff refresh after every prompt task terminates (success carries the message id; cancelled/error paths route through _send_terminal_event_and_refresh) and on the refresh_diff command from the control plane; a HTTP 404 from the diff endpoints marks the control plane unsupported and disables refresh for the rest of the sandbox's life.

Refresh failures are reported to POST /sessions/:id/diff/failure bounded to SESSION_DIFF_MAX_ERROR_LENGTH (2000) code points without crashing the bridge; close() stops accepting requests and bounds shutdown waiting to DIFF_REFRESH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (5 s), cancelling in-flight collection on timeout.

The sandbox uploads with Authorization Bearer <sandbox token> to PUT /sessions/{session_id}/diff and reports failures to POST /sessions/{session_id}/diff/failure; the client owns its httpx connection pool lazily (created on first request so a never-run bridge leaks nothing).

The central-router routes for diffs are: GET /sessions/:id/diff (user-or-service), PUT /sessions/:id/diff (sandbox-token with user-or-service fallback, body capped at SESSION_DIFF_UPLOAD_BODY_MAX_BYTES=1.5 MiB), POST /sessions/:id/diff/failure (sandbox-token, body capped at 16 KiB), GET /sessions/:id/diff/:revisionId/files/:fileId and POST /sessions/:id/diff/retry (user-or-service); bundle ids must match SESSION_DIFF_ID_PATTERN before forwarding since they are interpolated into internal route queries.

Internal diff paths (diffState, diffStore, diffFailure, diffResolveFile, diffRetry) are constants in SessionInternalPaths shared by the central router and the DO route table so the two sides cannot drift; the router validates bundle schemas once and the DO validates again on store.

SessionDiffsHandler maps domain errors to HTTP: invalid bundle / repository mismatch / baseline mismatch / invalid failure / invalid file identity → 400; baseline unavailable or sandbox not connected → 409; stale revision → 409 with code diff_revision_stale plus currentRevisionId; file not found → 404 with code diff_file_not_found plus currentRevisionId; unrecognized errors are rethrown.

SessionDiffService.publishBundle atomically publishes one latest bundle: it validates the upload schema, asserts the bundle repository set matches the session's repositories and every baseSha equals the pinned baseline (throwing DiffRepositoryMismatchError, DiffBaselineUnavailableError, or DiffBaselineMismatchError), then replaces the stored bundle and broadcasts diff_state_changed {revisionId, updatedAt} to all clients.

SessionDiffStore persists exactly one latest bundle in the session DO's embedded SQLite singleton row (session_diff with CHECK singleton = 1) holding revision_id, trigger_message_id, bundle_json, captured_at, last_error, error_at, updated_at; replaceBundle is a single UPSERT that clears any prior failure and recordFailure keeps the current bundle while storing the newest bounded error.
Store reads validate the bundle and failure columns independently: a corrupt bundle can never hide a real failure and corrupt failure metadata can never discard an otherwise readable bundle.

The public state never includes patch bodies: toSessionDiffManifest strips every patch before the browser boundary and re-validates with sessionDiffManifestSchema; patch bodies are served only by resolveFile which throws DiffRevisionStaleError when the revision is not the latest and DiffFileNotFoundError when the file is not a renderable patch of the current bundle.

The web client treats a stale-revision patch response (code diff_revision_stale) as a signal to re-fetch the latest manifest, so the selection identity (repository position + path) re-resolves against the new revision.

The shared zod schemas enforce structural rules protecting the wire and the routes: bundle version must equal SESSION_DIFF_VERSION, file ids must satisfy the route id pattern, paths must not contain NUL, oldPath is only valid for renamed files, renderable files must carry a patch and non-renderable files must not, per-file and aggregate patch byte limits, unique positions/identities/file ids/paths per bundle, and the fully encoded JSON bundle must fit SESSION_DIFF_MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES.

SESSION_DIFF_VERSION (1) is mirrored by hand between packages/shared/src/types/session-diffs.ts and diff_collector.py and must be kept in sync; SESSION_DIFF_MAX_ERROR_LENGTH (2000) is also mirrored, with a known astral-character divergence between Python code points and Zod UTF-16 units whose worst case is a rejected failure report degrading error display.

The web sidebar derives a Changes view model from the raw state with fixed precedence: hidden (no repository) → loading → error → unavailable (missing baseline) → working (agent processing; previous bundle stays visible) → failed (last refresh error, retry available) → available_after_execution → empty/ready; active execution outranks a previous failure.

useSessionDiffs polls GET /api/sessions/:id/diff and validates with sessionDiffStateSchema; useSessionDiffRetry POSTs /api/sessions/:id/diff/retry and revalidates the SWR key; session-changes-panel fetches per-file patches at /api/sessions/${sessionId}/diff/${revisionId}/files/${fileId} and renders them with a diff renderer, showing explanatory copy instead for binary, too_large, metadata_only, and submodule files.

Failure reporting is non-destructive end to end: the last good bundle remains current and resolvable while lastError (bounded message plus occurredAt) is surfaced with a retry action; the web view sets canRetry true only in the failed state.
